title: Homelessness in the US Fell the Most in More Than a Decade
summary: After years of climbing to record highs, the number of people without homes in the US fell by more than 6% in 2025 — about 49,000 fewer people. It is the second yearly drop in a row, after a smaller one in 2024. Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner shared the results of a yearly count of people in communities across the country. He said President Trump's steps to secure the border and make communities safer 'drove a historic decrease in homelessness.' A second study of the same count, from the group National Alliance to End Homelessness, found a similar drop but gave different reasons. Its leader, Ann Oliva, said Congress-funded programs are working and more people are getting housed. Both studies agree nearly 700,000 people in the US are still living in shelters or on the streets, far more than before the pandemic. The two sides disagree about what caused the drop. The Trump team points to its immigration changes, while Oliva says programs that house people first, without conditions, played a big part, especially for veterans.
why_it_matters: Even though the number fell, nearly 700,000 people in the US still have no home, and kids can learn how their community helps neighbors find a safe place to live.

background_read: Homelessness means not having a home to live in, so people sleep in shelters or on the streets.
Each year, communities across the country count how many people are without homes to see if the number is going up or down.
Some programs help by giving people a home first, without asking them to meet conditions first.
